content.text:
I've submitted index 5 (Bi 0.33, Fe 0.17, V 0.50) as the best composition: it gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 32.4 µA. I don't know how it compares with the best composition in the library.

| Index | Bi / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | 0.39 / 0.17 / 0.44 | 26.5 µA |
| 98 | 0.39 / 0.20 / 0.41 | 4.9 µA |
| 5 | 0.33 / 0.17 / 0.50 | 32.4 µA |

**How I chose:**
- **First pick:** I started near BiVO₄ (roughly equal Bi and V, least Fe), since that is the known photoanode in this system. The model check agreed: the predicted band gap for Fe₂O₃ is about 2.77 eV, right at the 2.72 eV light, so Fe-rich films should absorb poorly.
- **Second and third picks:** adding a little Fe and removing some V (index 98) cut the photocurrent about fivefold. So I moved the other way, to less Fe and more V (index 5), which scored higher.

**Limits of this result:**
- The merit budget allowed only three measurements. Nothing past index 5 in that direction was tested, such as index 24 (Bi 0.29, Fe 0.18, V 0.53), so the true best may lie further along it.
- I couldn't read the list of known crystal structures because the output was too large. The only structure I found for the model checks was Fe₂O₃. For the second and third measurements its band-gap predictions (0.89 and 0.81 eV) contradicted the first, so the required consultations there didn't really inform the choice.
- I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present in the measured spots is unconfirmed.
